name: Chapter 6: Permutations and Combinations
description: Counting principles, factorials, permutations with and without repetition, combinations, words, digits, committees, cards and exam techniques.

cards.term: State the fundamental (multiplication) principle of counting.
cards.definition: If one event can occur in m ways, and after it another event in n ways, the two together can occur in m × n ways. It extends to any number of events: m × n × p …

cards.term: Addition principle of counting?
cards.definition: If two tasks are mutually exclusive (you do one OR the other) and can be done in m and n ways, the total is m + n. Rule of thumb: AND → multiply, OR → add

cards.term: Multiplication principle: tree of 3 pants × 2 shirts
cards.definition: If one event can happen in m ways and then another in n ways, the pair can happen in m×n ways; 3 pants × 2 shirts = 6

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Multiplication principle · tree diagram

Mohan has 3 pants and 2 shirts. How many pant–shirt outfits? Draw the tree.

Each pant has how many shirt options?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Multiplication principle · tree diagram

Mohan has 3 pants and 2 shirts. How many pant–shirt outfits? Draw the tree.

Each of the 3 pants pairs with 2 shirts → 3 × 2 = 6 outfits. Choices in stages multiply.

For three stages (2 bags, 3 tiffin boxes, 2 bottles): 2 × 3 × 2 = 12.

cards.term: Sabnam has 2 school bags, 3 tiffin boxes and 2 water bottles (one of each). Number of ways?
cards.definition: 2 × 3 × 2 = 12

cards.term: Example 1: 4-letter words (with or without meaning) from the letters of ROSE, no repetition?
cards.definition: 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 24. With repetition allowed: 4 × 4 × 4 × 4 = 256

cards.term: Example 2: 4 flags of different colours; signals use 2 flags, one below the other. How many?
cards.definition: 4 × 3 = 12

cards.term: Example 3: 2-digit even numbers from 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 with repetition allowed?
cards.definition: Units: 2 or 4 (2 ways). Tens: any of 5. 2 × 5 = 10

cards.term: Slot method: fill the restricted position first
cards.definition: Even 3-digit numbers from 1..5 without repetition: units digit 2 or 4 (2 ways), then tens (4), then hundreds (3): 24; fill the restricted place first

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Slot method · restricted place first

How many 3-digit even numbers can be made from 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 with no repetition?

Which place has a condition?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Slot method · restricted place first

How many 3-digit even numbers can be made from 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 with no repetition?

Fill the restricted place first: the units digit must be 2 or 4 → 2 ways. Then the tens digit: 4 digits left. Then hundreds: 3 left.

2 × 4 × 3 = 24. If you fill hundreds first, the number of choices for the units digit depends on what you used: messy.

cards.term: Method: the slot (box) method for counting numbers or words.
cards.definition: 1) Draw one box per place. 2) Fill the boxes with a condition first (units digit even, first letter a vowel, leading digit ≠ 0). 3) Multiply the choices

cards.term: Example 4: signals with at least 2 of 5 different flags on a staff. How many?
cards.definition: 2 flags: 5·4 = 20; 3 flags: 5·4·3 = 60; 4 flags: 120; 5 flags: 120. Add (“or”): 320

cards.term: Ex 6.1 Q1: 3-digit numbers from 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 (i) with repetition (ii) without?
cards.definition: 125 (5 × 5 × 5) and 60 (5 × 4 × 3)

cards.term: Ex 6.1 Q2: 3-digit even numbers from 1–6 with repetition allowed?
cards.definition: Units 2, 4 or 6 (3 ways); tens 6; hundreds 6: 6 × 6 × 3 = 108

cards.term: Ex 6.1 Q3: 4-letter codes from the first 10 letters, no repetition?
cards.definition: 10 × 9 × 8 × 7 = 5040

cards.term: Ex 6.1 Q4: 5-digit phone numbers starting with 67, digits 0–9, no digit repeated?
cards.definition: Remaining 3 places from the 8 unused digits: 8 × 7 × 6 = 336

cards.term: Ex 6.1 Q5: a coin is tossed 3 times. Number of outcomes?
cards.definition: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8

cards.term: Ex 6.1 Q6: 5 flags of different colours; 2-flag signals?
cards.definition: 5 × 4 = 20

cards.term: Number of ways to answer 10 true/false questions?
cards.definition: 2¹⁰ = 1024

cards.term: Number of 3-digit numbers (any digits allowed)?
cards.definition: Hundreds 1–9 (9 ways), tens 10, units 10: 900. A leading 0 is not allowed

cards.term: Define a permutation.
cards.definition: An arrangement in a definite order of objects taken some or all at a time: order matters

cards.term: Theorem 1: number of permutations of n different objects taken r at a time (no repetition)?
Define n! and 0!.
cards.definition: n! = 1 × 2 × 3 × … × n, and 0! = 1 by definition. Also n! = n·(n − 1)!

cards.term: Why is 0! = 1?
cards.definition: ⁿPₙ = n!/0! must equal n! (arrange all n objects). Equivalently there is exactly one way to arrange nothing

cards.term: Example 5: evaluate 5!, 7!, 7! − 5!.
cards.definition: 120, 5040, 4920
7 × 6 = 42; (12 × 11)/2 = 66
No: 6 + 24 = 30 but 7! = 5040. Factorials do not add or multiply term by term

cards.term: Trap: is (m + n)! = m! + n!, or (2n)! = 2·n!?
cards.definition: Neither. e.g. (2·3)! = 720 but 2·3! = 12
(8 × 7)/2 = 28

cards.term: Example 7: evaluate n!/(r!(n − r)!) for n = 5, r = 2.
Example 8: 1/8! + 1/9! = x/10!. Find x.
Ex 6.2 Q5: evaluate n!/(n − r)! for n = 6, r = 2 and n = 9, r = 5.
cards.definition: 30 (6 × 5) and 15120 (9 × 8 × 7 × 6 × 5)

cards.term: ⁿP₀, ⁿP₁, ⁿPₙ₋₁ and ⁿPₙ?
cards.definition:
1, n, n!, n!
ⁿPₙ₋₁ = n!/1! = n!

cards.term: Theorem 2: permutations of n different objects taken r at a time with repetition allowed?
cards.definition: nʳ (each of the r places can be filled in n ways)

cards.term: Chairman and vice-chairman from 12 persons (one person, one post)?
cards.definition: ¹²P₂ = 12 × 11 = 132

cards.term: Ex 6.3 Q5: chairman and vice-chairman from a committee of 8?
cards.definition: ⁸P₂ = 8 × 7 = 56

cards.term: Ex 6.3 Q1–2: 3-digit numbers from 1–9 with no repetition; 4-digit numbers with no repeated digit?
cards.definition: ⁹P₃ = 504. 4-digit: first digit 9 ways (not 0), then 9, 8, 7: 9 × 9 × 8 × 7 = 4536

cards.term: Trap: “4-digit numbers with no digit repeated”. Is the answer ¹⁰P₄?
cards.definition: No. ¹⁰P₄ = 5040 includes numbers starting with 0. Subtract them: 5040 − ⁹P₃ = 5040 − 504 = 4536

cards.term: Ex 6.3 Q3: 3-digit even numbers from 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, no repetition?
cards.definition: Units 2, 4 or 6 (3 ways); tens 5; hundreds 4: 3 × 5 × 4 = 60

cards.term: Ex 6.3 Q4: 4-digit numbers from 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, no repetition. How many are even?
cards.definition: ⁵P₄ = 120. Even: units 2 or 4 (2 ways) then 4 × 3 × 2: 48

cards.term: Example 10 and 11: 4-digit numbers from 1–9 without repetition; numbers between 100 and 1000 from 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 without repetition?
cards.definition: ⁹P₄ = 3024. Second: ⁶P₃ − ⁵P₂ = 120 − 20 = 100 (subtract those with 0 in the hundreds place)

cards.term: Ex 6.3 Q8: words using all letters of EQUATION once each?
cards.definition: 8! = 40320

cards.term: Ex 6.3 Q9: words from MONDAY, no repetition: (i) 4 letters (ii) all letters (iii) all letters, first letter a vowel?
cards.definition: (i) ⁶P₄ = 360 (ii) 6! = 720 (iii) vowels O or A: 2 × 5! = 240

cards.term: Example 12(i): find n if ⁿP₅ = 42 · ⁿP₃ (n > 4).
cards.definition: Divide by n(n − 1)(n − 2): (n − 3)(n − 4) = 42 → n² − 7n − 30 = 0 → (n − 10)(n + 3) = 0 → n = 10 (n = −3 rejected)

cards.term: Example 12(ii): find n if ⁿP₄ / ⁿ⁻¹P₄ = 5/3 (n > 4).
cards.definition: ⁿP₄/ⁿ⁻¹P₄ = n/(n − 4) after cancelling (n − 1)(n − 2)(n − 3). So 3n = 5(n − 4) → n = 10

cards.term: Method: solving equations with nPr.
cards.definition: Write each ⁿPᵣ as a product (n)(n − 1)…, cancel the common factors after checking they are non-zero (n > r), solve the resulting polynomial, then reject values that violate n ≥ r, n, r ∈ N

cards.term: Ex 6.3 Q6: find n if ⁿ⁻¹P₃ : ⁿP₄ = 1 : 9.
cards.definition: \(\dfrac{(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)}{n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)} = \dfrac1n = \dfrac19\) → n = 9

cards.term: Example 13: 5·⁴Pᵣ = 6·⁵Pᵣ₋₁. Find r.
cards.definition: Algebra gives (6 − r)(5 − r) = 6 → r² − 11r + 24 = 0 → r = 3 or 8. But ⁴Pᵣ needs r ≤ 4, so r = 3 only. Check: 5·24 = 120 = 6·20

cards.term: Correction: NCERT Example 13 ends with “r = 8, 3”. Is r = 8 valid?
cards.definition: No. ⁴P₈ does not exist (r cannot exceed n = 4). Always test roots against the conditions r ≤ n. The correct answer is r = 3

cards.term: Ex 6.3 Q7: find r if (i) ⁵Pᵣ = 2·⁶Pᵣ₋₁, (ii) ⁵Pᵣ = ⁶Pᵣ₋₁.
cards.definition: (i) (7 − r)(6 − r) = 12 → r² − 13r + 30 = 0 → r = 3 or 10; r ≤ 5 → r = 3. (ii) (7 − r)(6 − r) = 6 → r² − 13r + 36 = 0 → r = 4 or 9 → r = 4

cards.term: Permutations of n objects when p of them are alike and the rest different?
Permutations of n objects with p₁ alike of one kind, p₂ of another, …, pₖ of the k-th kind?
cards.definition: \(\dfrac{n!}{p_1!\,p_2!\cdots p_k!}\)

cards.term: Why divide by p! for identical objects?
cards.definition: Treating the p alike objects as different overcounts: every real arrangement is counted p! times (the alike ones can be shuffled among themselves without any visible change)

cards.term: Arrangements of the letters of ROOT?
cards.definition: 4!/2! = 12

cards.term: Arrangements of the letters of INSTITUTE?
cards.definition: 9 letters: I twice, T three times → 9!/(2!·3!) = 30240

cards.term: Example 9: permutations of the letters of ALLAHABAD?
cards.definition: 9 letters: A four times, L twice → 9!/(4!·2!) = 7560

cards.term: Example 15: 4 red, 3 yellow and 2 green discs in a row (same colour identical)?
Number of arrangements of the letters of MISSISSIPPI?
Ex 6.3 Q10: in how many of them do the four I’s not come together?
cards.definition: Together: treat IIII as one letter: 8!/(4!·2!) = 840. So 34650 − 840 = 33810

cards.term: Method: “vowels always together”.
cards.definition: Tie the vowels into one block. Arrange the block with the other letters, then multiply by the arrangements inside the block

cards.term: Method: “vowels never together”.
cards.definition: Total − (vowels together). Complement counting is faster than direct counting

cards.term: Example 14: 8-letter arrangements of DAUGHTER with (i) all vowels together (ii) not together?
cards.definition: (i) block AUE + 5 letters = 6 objects: 6!·3! = 4320. (ii) 8! − 4320 = 36000

cards.term: Example 16: INDEPENDENCE has 12 letters (N ×3, E ×4, D ×2). Total, and words starting with P?
cards.definition: 12!/(3!·4!·2!) = 1663200. Start with P: 11!/(3!·4!·2!) = 138600

cards.term: Example 16(ii)–(iv): INDEPENDENCE: vowels together; vowels never together; begin with I and end with P?
cards.definition: Vowels EEEEI form a block: 8!/(3!·2!) × 5!/4! = 16800. Never together: 1663200 − 16800 = 1646400. I first, P last: 10!/(3!·2!·4!) = 12600

cards.term: Ex 6.3 Q11: PERMUTATIONS (12 letters, T twice) with (i) P first and S last (ii) vowels together (iii) exactly 4 letters between P and S?
cards.definition: (i) 10!/2! = 1814400. (ii) 5 vowels as a block: 8!/2! × 5! = 2419200. (iii) P and S can sit in 7 position-pairs (1–6, 2–7, …, 7–12), in 2 orders: 14 × 10!/2! = 25401600

cards.term: Example 22: rank of a word. AGAIN in dictionary order: how many words, and what is the 50th?
cards.definition: 5!/2! = 60 words. Starting with A: 4! = 24; G: 4!/2! = 12; I: 12 → 48. Next letter N: 49th NAAGI, 50th NAAIG

cards.term: Method: rank of a word in dictionary order.
cards.definition: Sort the letters. For each position count the words that start with every smaller letter (with the correct repeated-letter division), add them up, and add 1

cards.term: Misc Q4: EXAMINATION arranged as in a dictionary: how many words come before the first word starting with E?
cards.definition: Only words starting with A come before E. Fix A: remaining 10 letters with I ×2, N ×2: 10!/(2!·2!) = 907200

cards.term: Example 23: numbers greater than 1000000 using the digits 1, 2, 0, 2, 4, 2, 4?
cards.definition: All 7-digit arrangements: 7!/(3!·2!) = 420, minus those starting with 0: 6!/(3!·2!) = 60 → 360

cards.term: Misc Q11: arrangements of ASSASSINATION with all S’s together?
cards.definition: 13 letters: A ×3, S ×4, I ×2, N ×2. Block SSSS + 9 others = 10 objects: 10!/(3!·2!·2!) = 151200

cards.term: Define a combination. Permutation vs combination?
cards.definition: A selection where order does not matter. Permutation: arrangement (order matters). Memory: P = Position, C = Committee

cards.term: Permutation or combination?
cards.definition: Forming a 3-letter word: P; Choosing a team of 3 players: C; Seating 5 people in a row: P; Handshakes among 12 people: C; A 4-digit PIN: P; Selecting 5 cards from a pack: C; President and secretary from 10: P; Chords joining 7 points on a circle: C

cards.term: Formula for ⁿCᵣ?
Relation between ⁿPᵣ and ⁿCᵣ?
cards.definition: \({}^nP_r = {}^nC_r \times r!\): choose the r objects, then arrange them in r! ways

cards.term: ⁿC₀, ⁿC₁, ⁿCₙ?
cards.definition: 1, n, 1

cards.term: Why is ⁿC₀ = 1?
cards.definition: Choosing nothing can be done in exactly one way (leave everything behind)

cards.term: Theorem: ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₙ₋ᵣ. Meaning?
cards.definition: Selecting r objects to take is the same as selecting n − r objects to leave behind

cards.term: ⁿCₐ = ⁿC_b implies?
cards.definition: a = b or a + b = n

cards.term: Theorem 6 (Pascal’s rule): ⁿCᵣ + ⁿCᵣ₋₁ = ?
cards.definition: ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ. Proof by writing both over r!(n − r + 1)! or by “is a particular object chosen or not”

cards.term: Pascal’s triangle and Pascal’s rule
cards.definition: Each entry of Pascal’s triangle is the sum of the two above: nCr + nC(r−1) = (n+1)Cr; rows are symmetric and sum to 2^n

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Pascal’s triangle · nCr

Build Pascal’s triangle. How does it prove ⁿCᵣ + ⁿCᵣ₋₁ = ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ?

Add the two numbers above.
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Pascal’s triangle · nCr

Build Pascal’s triangle. How does it prove ⁿCᵣ + ⁿCᵣ₋₁ = ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ?

Each entry = the sum of the two above it: 5 + 10 = 15 → ⁵C₁ + ⁵C₂ = ⁶C₂.

Rows are symmetric (ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₙ₋ᵣ) and row n sums to 2ⁿ (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64).

cards.term: Example 17: if ⁹Cᵣ = ⁹Cᵣ₋₁ … i.e. ⁿC₉ = ⁿC₈, find ⁿC₁₇.
cards.definition: Equal values → 9 + 8 = n → n = 17, so ⁿC₁₇ = ¹⁷C₁₇ = 1

cards.term: Ex 6.4 Q1: if ⁿC₈ = ⁿC₂, find ⁿC₂.
cards.definition: n = 8 + 2 = 10 → ¹⁰C₂ = 45

cards.term: Ex 6.4 Q2: find n if ²ⁿC₃ : ⁿC₃ = 12 : 1 and = 11 : 1.
cards.definition: ²ⁿC₃/ⁿC₃ = 4(2n − 1)/(n − 2). For 12: 8n − 4 = 12n − 24 → n = 5. For 11: 8n − 4 = 11n − 22 → n = 6

cards.term: Chords through 21 points on a circle?
cards.definition: ²¹C₂ = 210. In general n points give ⁿC₂ chords (handshake count)

cards.term: Ex 6.4 Q4: team of 3 boys and 3 girls from 5 boys and 4 girls?
cards.definition: ⁵C₃ × ⁴C₃ = 10 × 4 = 40

cards.term: Ex 6.4 Q5: choose 9 balls from 6 red, 5 white, 5 blue with 3 of each colour?
cards.definition: ⁶C₃ × ⁵C₃ × ⁵C₃ = 20 × 10 × 10 = 2000

cards.term: Ex 6.4 Q6 and Misc Q8: 5-card hands with exactly one ace (or exactly one king)?
cards.definition: ⁴C₁ × ⁴⁸C₄ = 4 × 194580 = 778320

cards.term: Ex 6.4 Q7: cricket team of 11 from 17 players (5 can bowl) with exactly 4 bowlers?
cards.definition: ⁵C₄ × ¹²C₇ = 5 × 792 = 3960

cards.term: Ex 6.4 Q8: 2 black and 3 red balls from 5 black and 6 red?
cards.definition: ⁵C₂ × ⁶C₃ = 10 × 20 = 200

cards.term: Ex 6.4 Q9: 5 courses from 9, two specific courses compulsory?
cards.definition: Choose the other 3 from 7: ⁷C₃ = 35

cards.term: Example 18: committee of 3 from 2 men and 3 women. Total, and with 1 man and 2 women?
cards.definition: ⁵C₃ = 10; ²C₁ × ³C₂ = 6

cards.term: Example 19: 4 cards from 52. Total number of hands?
cards.definition: ⁵²C₄ = 270725

cards.term: Example 19: 4 cards (i) same suit (ii) one from each suit (iii) all face cards?
cards.definition: (i) 4 × ¹³C₄ = 2860 (ii) 13⁴ = 28561 (iii) ¹²C₄ = 495

cards.term: Example 19: 4 cards (iv) two red and two black (v) all the same colour?
cards.definition: (iv) ²⁶C₂ × ²⁶C₂ = 325² = 105625 (v) 2 × ²⁶C₄ = 29900

cards.term: Example 20: words of 3 vowels and 2 consonants from INVOLUTE (4 vowels, 4 consonants)?
cards.definition: Select: ⁴C₃ × ⁴C₂ = 24; arrange each in 5! ways: 24 × 120 = 2880. Select first, then arrange

cards.term: Example 21: 5-member team from 4 girls and 7 boys: (i) no girl (ii) at least one boy and one girl (iii) at least 3 girls?
cards.definition: (i) ⁷C₅ = 21. (ii) 7 + 84 + 210 + 140 = 441 (or ¹¹C₅ − 21 = 462 − 21 = 441). (iii) ⁴C₃·⁷C₂ + ⁴C₄·⁷C₁ = 84 + 7 = 91

cards.term: Trap: “at least one boy and one girl”. Fastest method?
cards.definition: Total − (all boys) − (all girls) = ¹¹C₅ − ⁷C₅ − 0 = 462 − 21 = 441 (no all-girl team: only 4 girls)

cards.term: Method: “at least” and “at most” selection problems.
cards.definition: Either add the separate cases, or use total − the opposite cases (whichever has fewer cases). For “at least k”, the complement is “fewer than k”

cards.term: Misc Q1: words of 2 vowels and 3 consonants from DAUGHTER?
cards.definition: Vowels A, U, E; consonants 5: ³C₂ × ⁵C₃ × 5! = 3 × 10 × 120 = 3600

cards.term: Misc Q2: words using all letters of EQUATION with vowels together and consonants together?
cards.definition: Two blocks can be ordered in 2! ways; vowels 5! ; consonants 3!: 2 × 120 × 6 = 1440

cards.term: Misc Q3: committee of 7 from 9 boys and 4 girls: (i) exactly 3 girls (ii) at least 3 girls (iii) at most 3 girls?
cards.definition: (i) ⁴C₃·⁹C₄ = 504 (ii) 504 + ⁴C₄·⁹C₃ = 504 + 84 = 588 (iii) ¹³C₇ − 84 = 1716 − 84 = 1632

cards.term: Misc Q5: 6-digit numbers from 0, 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, divisible by 10, no repetition?
cards.definition: Last digit must be 0; arrange the other five: 5! = 120

cards.term: Misc Q6: words with 2 different vowels and 2 different consonants from the English alphabet (5 vowels, 21 consonants)?
cards.definition: ⁵C₂ × ²¹C₂ × 4! = 10 × 210 × 24 = 50400

cards.term: Misc Q7: attempt 8 of 12 questions (Part I: 5, Part II: 7) with at least 3 from each part?
cards.definition: (3,5): ⁵C₃·⁷C₅ = 210; (4,4): ⁵C₄·⁷C₄ = 175; (5,3): ⁵C₅·⁷C₃ = 35. Total 420

cards.term: Misc Q9: 5 men and 4 women in a row with women in the even places?
cards.definition: 4 even places (2, 4, 6, 8) for the women: 4!; the 5 other places for the men: 5!. 24 × 120 = 2880

cards.term: Misc Q10: choose 10 of 25 students; 3 of them will all join or all stay out.
cards.definition: All three join: ²²C₇; none joins: ²²C₁₀. 170544 + 646646 = 817190

cards.term: Example 24: 5 girls and 3 boys in a row, no two boys together?
cards.definition: Girls first: 5!; boys into 3 of the 6 gaps: ⁶P₃. 120 × 120 = 14400

cards.term: Gaps method: no two boys together (Example 24)
cards.definition: 5 girls in 5! ways create 6 gaps; choose and order 3 gaps for the boys: 6P3; total 5!·6P3 = 14400

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Gaps method · no two together

5 girls and 3 boys sit in a row so that no two boys are together. How many arrangements?

Seat the girls first. How many gaps do they make?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Gaps method · no two together

5 girls and 3 boys sit in a row so that no two boys are together. How many arrangements?

Seat the girls first: 5! ways. They create 6 gaps (×) including both ends. Boys go into 3 different gaps, in order: ⁶P₃ = 120.

Total 5! × ⁶P₃ = 14400. Method for “not together”: arrange the others first, then insert.

cards.term: Circular permutations: (n − 1)!
cards.definition: n people around a round table: (n−1)! arrangements, since rotations are equal (fix one person); necklace/garland with flipping: (n−1)!/2

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Circular arrangements · beyond the textbook

In how many ways can 4 people sit around a round table?

Do rotations count as different?
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Circular arrangements · beyond the textbook

In how many ways can 4 people sit around a round table?

Turning everyone one seat round gives the same arrangement (same neighbours). The 4 rotations count as one.

So fix one person and arrange the other 3: (4 − 1)! = 6. In general (n − 1)!; for necklaces (which can be flipped) (n − 1)!/2.

cards.term: Necklace or garland of n different beads?
cards.definition: \(\dfrac{(n-1)!}{2}\): a necklace can be flipped over, so clockwise and anticlockwise orders coincide

cards.term: Selecting any number (≥ 1) of n different objects?
cards.definition: 2ⁿ − 1: each object is in or out, minus the empty selection

cards.term: Number of selections of r objects when repetition allowed / non-negative integral solutions of x₁ + … + xᵣ = n?
cards.definition: \({}^{n+r-1}C_{r-1}\) (stars and bars). Example: x + y + z = 10 has ¹²C₂ = 66 solutions

cards.term: Number of positive integral solutions of x₁ + x₂ + … + xᵣ = n?
Number of diagonals of a convex n-gon?
cards.definition: \({}^nC_2 - n = \dfrac{n(n-3)}{2}\). Hexagon: 9

cards.term: Number of triangles from n points, no three collinear? With p points collinear?
cards.definition: ⁿC₃; with p collinear: ⁿC₃ − ᵖC₃

cards.term: Number of lines from n points, no three collinear? With p collinear?
cards.definition: ⁿC₂; with p collinear: ⁿC₂ − ᵖC₂ + 1

cards.term: Rectangles in an 8 × 8 chessboard?
cards.definition: Choose 2 of 9 horizontal lines and 2 of 9 vertical: ⁹C₂ × ⁹C₂ = 36² = 1296. Squares: 1² + 2² + … + 8² = 204

cards.term: Number of divisors of N = p^a · q^b · r^c?
cards.definition: (a + 1)(b + 1)(c + 1). Example: 360 = 2³·3²·5 has 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 divisors

cards.term: Dividing 8 people into two equal groups of 4 (unlabelled) versus two named teams?
cards.definition: Named teams: ⁸C₄ = 70. Unlabelled groups: ⁸C₄/2! = 35. Divide by (number of equal groups)! when the groups are indistinguishable

cards.term: Derangements (nobody gets their own item): D₃ and D₄?
cards.definition: D₃ = 2, D₄ = 9 (formula Dₙ = n!(1 − 1/1! + 1/2! − … ± 1/n!))

cards.term: Identities: r·ⁿCᵣ and ⁿPᵣ in terms of smaller cases?
cards.definition: r · ⁿCᵣ = n · ⁿ⁻¹Cᵣ₋₁; ⁿPᵣ = n · ⁿ⁻¹Pᵣ₋₁; ⁿCᵣ = (n/r) · ⁿ⁻¹Cᵣ₋₁

cards.term: Sum of ⁿC₀ + ⁿC₁ + … + ⁿCₙ?
cards.definition: 2ⁿ (all subsets); alternating sum ⁿC₀ − ⁿC₁ + … = 0 for n ≥ 1; sum of even-indexed = sum of odd-indexed = 2ⁿ⁻¹

cards.term: Hockey-stick identity: ʳCᵣ + ʳ⁺¹Cᵣ + … + ⁿCᵣ?
cards.definition: ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ₊₁. e.g. ²C₂ + ³C₂ + ⁴C₂ + ⁵C₂ = 1 + 3 + 6 + 10 = 20 = ⁶C₃

cards.term: In how many ways can 10 identical sweets be distributed among 4 children (any child may get none)?
cards.definition: \({}^{13}C_3 = 286\) (stars and bars with n = 10, r = 4)

cards.term: Number of ways to arrange the letters of BANANA so that no two A’s are adjacent?
cards.definition: Arrange B, N, N: 3!/2! = 3 ways; they make 4 gaps; choose 3 gaps for the A’s: ⁴C₃ = 4. Total 3 × 4 = 12

cards.term: Number of 5-digit numbers divisible by 5 using digits 0–9 (any repetition)?
cards.definition: Units 0 or 5 (2 ways), first digit 1–9 (9 ways), middle three 10³: 9 × 10 × 10 × 10 × 2 = 18000

cards.term:
MCQ: The value of ⁵P₃ is
(a) 10 (b) 60 (c) 120 (d) 15
cards.definition: (b) 60 = 5 × 4 × 3

cards.term:
MCQ: If ⁿC₁₀ = ⁿC₁₂, then n =
(a) 22 (b) 2 (c) 12 (d) 10
cards.definition: (a) 22 since 10 + 12 = n

cards.term:
MCQ: The number of ways to arrange the letters of the word LEVEL is
(a) 120 (b) 60 (c) 30 (d) 24
cards.definition: 5!/(2!·2!) = (c) 30

cards.term:
MCQ: A committee of 3 is chosen from 5 people. Number of ways?
(a) 60 (b) 10 (c) 20 (d) 15
cards.definition: ⁵C₃ = (b) 10

cards.term:
MCQ: If ⁿP₂ = 20, then n =
(a) 4 (b) 5 (c) 6 (d) 10
cards.definition: n(n − 1) = 20 → (b) 5

cards.term:
MCQ: The number of 3-digit numbers with distinct digits is
(a) 720 (b) 648 (c) 900 (d) 504
cards.definition: 9 × 9 × 8 = (b) 648

cards.term:
MCQ: ⁿCᵣ + ⁿCᵣ₋₁ equals
(a) ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ (b) ⁿCᵣ₊₁ (c) ⁿ⁻¹Cᵣ (d) 2ⁿCᵣ
cards.definition: (a): Pascal’s rule

cards.term: Integer answer (JEE Main): number of 4-letter words (any letters) from the letters of MATH with no letter repeated?
cards.definition: 24 (4!)

cards.term: Integer answer: the number of straight lines joining 8 points, of which 3 are collinear?
cards.definition: ⁸C₂ − ³C₂ + 1 = 28 − 3 + 1 = 26

cards.term: Integer answer: number of diagonals of a decagon?
cards.definition: 10 × 7/2 = 35

cards.term:
Assertion–Reason.
A: ⁿPᵣ ≥ ⁿCᵣ.
R: ⁿPᵣ = r! · ⁿCᵣ.
(a) Both true, R explains A (b) Both true, R does not explain A (c) A true, R false (d) A false, R true
cards.definition: (a): r! ≥ 1

cards.term:
Assertion–Reason.
A: The number of subsets of a set of 5 elements is 32.
R: ⁵C₀ + ⁵C₁ + … + ⁵C₅ = 2⁵.
(a) Both true, R explains A (b) Both true, R does not explain A (c) A false, R true (d) Both false
cards.definition: (a)

cards.term: True/False: ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₛ implies r = s.
cards.definition: False: it also holds when r + s = n (e.g. ⁸C₃ = ⁸C₅)

cards.term: Case-based: a school has 6 teachers and 8 students for a 5-member panel with exactly 2 teachers. In how many ways?
cards.definition: ⁶C₂ × ⁸C₃ = 15 × 56 = 840

cards.term: Case-based: a PIN has 4 digits (0–9), repetition allowed, and the first digit is not 0. How many PINs?
cards.definition: 9 × 10 × 10 × 10 = 9000

cards.term: 3-mark: how many 4-digit numbers greater than 5000 can be formed from 3, 5, 6, 7, 9 with no repetition?
cards.definition: Thousands digit 5, 6, 7 or 9 (4 ways), then 4 × 3 × 2: 4 × 24 = 96

cards.term: 4-mark: 5 boys and 4 girls form a team of 5 with at least 2 girls. How many teams?
cards.definition: Total ⁹C₅ = 126 minus (0 girls: ⁵C₅ = 1) minus (1 girl: ⁴C₁·⁵C₄ = 20) = 105
